<description>
While our best header is below `-minimumchainwork`, a peer's headers first go through the PRESYNC phase of `HeadersSyncState`, and none of them are stored. So `pindexBestKnownBlock` stays null for the peer we're syncing from, and `ConsiderEviction` (net_processing.cpp:5504) treats it like an outbound peer that never announced a block:

1. it starts `CHAIN_SYNC_TIMEOUT` (20 min)
2. it sends a getheaders to "verify chain work"
3. after `HEADERS_RESPONSE_TIME` it disconnects with `Outbound peer has old chain, best known block = <none>`

This happens even though the peer is still sending headers. The presync progress is lost and the next peer starts from scratch.

On mainnet presync is roughly 480 headers round trips. If that takes more than ~22 minutes (about 2.5 s per round trip, e.g. over slow Tor or I2P), the sync peer gets evicted before presync can finish, and the same thing can happen with the next peer. The chain sync logic is from #11490, presync came later in #25717, and the two were never connected.

The timeout is not reset on presync work alone. When it is set, the work the peer has shown during presync is recorded, and when it expires the timeout is renewed for another `CHAIN_SYNC_TIMEOUT` only if that work has increased since. A peer that stops sending headers is therefore still asked once with getheaders and then disconnected, within about two periods (~42 minutes), as before. `m_headers_sync_mutex` is never held while taking `cs_main`, and `p2p_headers_sync_with_minchainwork.py` and `p2p_sendheaders.py` also pass with `DEBUG_LOCKORDER`.

The new `test_presync_peer_not_evicted` in `p2p_headers_sync_with_minchainwork.py` restarts a node with `-minimumchainwork=0x20000` (65536 headers). An outbound peer then sends it one full headers message per mocked minute for 25 minutes, so presync is still running at the end. On master the peer is disconnected after 24 minutes. With the fix it stays connected and `presynced_headers` keeps going up. `p2p_outbound_eviction.py`, `p2p_eviction.py` and `feature_minchainwork.py` still pass.

`test_presync_peer_stalled_is_evicted` covers the other side: a single outbound peer sends one headers message and then only answers pings, and it is disconnected after about 42 minutes of mocktime. That test fails without the progress check.
</description>

[2026-10-14] c:6161235415 comment by cyb3ralbert (contributor):
Tested 34ef37a (also merged with master 8406af1c).

The new test passes on this PR but fails on master. With a single outbound peer, a peer that sends one headers message and then stops responding to `getheaders` remains connected for 24 hours under mocktime, whereas master disconnects it after 24 minutes. The peer still responds to pings.

With a second outbound peer, the headers download timeout fires after 29 minutes, for the slow peer as well.

Could we reset the timeout only when presync work has increased since the previous timeout checkpoint? This might preserve the intended behavior for slow peers without allowing a stalled peer to hold the only outbound slot.

A couple of questions:
- Is the Tor/I2P latency scenario expected to apply when this is the only outbound peer?
- Was the eviction observed on a real node, or inferred from expected round-trip times?
[2026-10-14] c:6163775056 comment by 0xShadowX:
Thanks for testing, and you're right: resetting whenever presync work was at least the tip's work let a stalled peer hold the slot indefinitely.

Pushed bf56f4fb83. The presync work is now recorded when the timeout is set, and when it expires the timeout is only renewed if that work has increased since. Otherwise it goes through the usual getheaders and disconnect. A new test, `test_presync_peer_stalled_is_evicted`, sends one headers message and then only answers pings; the peer is disconnected after ~42 minutes of mocktime (one renewal because of the first headers, then the normal timeout), and the test fails on the previous revision.

On the questions:
- Single outbound peer: nothing in the logic depends on how many outbound peers there are, so a slow Tor/I2P link can hit it with one peer as well, and then it has no other peer to fall back on. I haven't measured that case.
- Real node: no, the eviction was not observed on a real node. It is inferred from the ~480 presync round trips on mainnet against the ~22 minute window, and reproduced with mocktime in the functional test.
</new_statements>
